root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `njs_lexer_multi()` evaluates another conditional-token lookahead, it must prove `lexer->start < lexer->end`. The vulnerable lexer enters the loop for the tail-boundary `?` case without that conjunct and can therefore dereference `lexer->start[0]` at the exclusive end pointer.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is the missing end-of-buffer guard on the conditional-token lookahead loop. On the crashing lone-`?` witness, the final in-bounds `?` already advanced `lexer->start` to `lexer->end`, but `njs_lexer_multi()` still proceeds toward the lookahead read because its loop condition checks only `length != 0 && multi != NULL`.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The authoritative fixed original is guarded on the saved lone-`?` input, so the required assertion is differentially verified with the adjacent `append_second_question_at_eof` perturbation, where one real lookahead byte remains and the protected read executes under the fixed guard.

nodes.state: At the selected tail-boundary conditional lookahead, `njs_lexer_multi()` executes `c = lexer->start[0];` with `lexer->start == lexer->end`, so the read dereferences the exclusive end pointer of the script buffer.

On the selected tail-boundary `?` dispatch, `njs_lexer_next_token()` has already consumed the final in-bounds `?`, so the cursor handed to `njs_lexer_multi()` is already exhausted (`lexer->start == lexer->end`).

edges.relation: The same exhausted lexer cursor value selected at the tail-boundary conditional dispatch is passed unchanged into `njs_lexer_multi()` and becomes the missing-guard operand at the loop entry.
